assumptions.name: Non-SiPho specialty foundry base

entries.subject: STMicroelectronics N.V.

stage2.note: Revenue beat of +1.5% vs consensus ($3,095M vs $3,050M). At 50% surprise probability and 'noise' label, the marginal beat is consistent with calibrated uncertainty. Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.13. No methodology change warranted.

assumptions.name: Automotive/P&D stabilisation
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: EU car registrations -3.9% YoY in January, -1.2% YoY YTD February. Infineon remains cautious on automotive. ST started from a weaker base than peers, with P&D -31.6% YoY in Q4.
assumptions.miss_reason: Revenue threshold met ($389M >= $380M) despite continued operational weakness. P&D operating loss deepened from -$28M to -$84M YoY, confirming directional concern but not the revenue-based testable question.

lessons_learned: P&D segment revenue threshold was met despite severe operational deterioration (operating loss -$84M vs -$28M YoY). Revenue-based testable questions can miss profitability erosion — noted as observation, no methodology change.

Skalierungslogik confirmed: P&D at 12.4% segment share correctly scaled mismatch to ~2.5pp at group level, which did not produce a group-level signal. AM&S (+23.2% YoY) and EMP (+31.3% YoY) overcompensated.
50% probability / 'noise' label produced Brier component of 0.25 — neutral, no calibration damage. Correct restraint.

score_summary.stage2_note: Segment share 12.4% scales -20pp P&D mismatch down to -2.5pp at group level. Blind spot is real but mechanically too small to produce a group-level signal.

entries.subject: GE Vernova Inc.

stage2.note: GAAP EPS of $17.44 includes $3.99B pre-tax gain from Prolec GE remeasurement and $330M from Proficy divestiture (non-operating, non-recurring). Adjusted EPS reconstructed from Adjusted EBITDA of $896M, D&A of $341M, non-operating benefit income of $134M, and 272M diluted shares yields approximately $1.97–$2.16 depending on effective tax rate assumption (midpoint ~$2.06). Beat of roughly 15% vs $1.79 consensus. Self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — system correctly refrained from claiming a strong signal.

assumptions.name: Gas Power demand trajectory
assumptions.condition_met_note: Below threshold by $29M (0.6%) — de minimis deviation, materially aligned with 'no mismatch' call.

assumptions.name: Wind segment loss trajectory
assumptions.testable_question: Wind segment EBITDA better than -$150M in Q1?
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: BOEM suspended Vineyard Wind, Revolution Wind, Sunrise Wind. Weak onshore orders from US policy uncertainty. Tariff impact $300-400M guided for full year.
assumptions.magnitude_note: Actual result $232M worse than threshold and $218M worse than guided full-year Wind loss of roughly -$400M after just one quarter — deterioration substantially more severe than anticipated.

lessons_learned: Stage 1 correctly resolved all three assumption calls — two aligned (Power marginally below threshold but de minimis; Electrification clearly above), one material mismatch (Wind) confirmed with severity exceeding expectation.
Wind mismatch validates the Tetlock-style edge-seeking approach: the analysis identified a blind spot in consensus guidance and was directionally correct with meaningful magnitude.

Stage 2 miss on direction was correctly self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — confidence calibration held. The Prolec-GE remeasurement gain of $3.99B was a bookkeeping event not foreseeable at analysis time and does not materially affect Adjusted EPS comparison.

GAAP vs. Adjusted EPS distinction is critical for resolution: headline GAAP of $17.44 would falsely suggest a 874% beat; reconstructed Adjusted EPS of ~$2.00 shows a more modest 10–20% beat vs consensus.

entries.subject: onsemi (ON Semiconductor Corporation)

stage2.note: Non-GAAP diluted EPS $0.64 vs consensus $0.62 — beat of approximately 3.2%, well within the consensus spread of $0.59–$0.66. Group revenue of $1,513M came in above the guidance midpoint of $1,485M; Non-GAAP gross margin landed at 38.5%. Self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability with a gap of only 5pp from neutral — system correctly refrained from claiming a directional signal. The marginal beat in the opposite direction is consistent with calibrated uncertainty on a noise-classified call.

assumptions.name: Automotive demand stability
assumptions.resolution_note: onsemi reorganised reporting segments to PSG/AMG/ISG; Automotive end-market revenue is no longer disclosed as a standalone figure. AMG (which contains automotive analog and mixed-signal exposure) reported $540M, down 3% QoQ. Management qualitatively cited 900V EV architecture wins with Geely and NIO and continued Treo-based design momentum, with no indication of automotive demand deterioration. Aligned-call cannot be formally resolved against the original threshold but qualitative evidence is consistent with the original verdict.

assumptions.name: Industrial stabilisation
assumptions.mismatch_drivers: Infineon Core Industrial GIP -21% sequentially, flat recovery only. ST Industrial still declining in FY25. PMI >50 but decelerating. Microchip and NXP show mixed signals. External evidence points to shallow, uneven industrial recovery insufficient to support near-stable Industrial revenue.
assumptions.actual_value: Not separately reported (segment restructuring); group revenue $1,513M above midpoint, Q2 guidance raised to $1,535–1,635M
assumptions.miss_reason: The material_mismatch could not be formally resolved against the original threshold because onsemi reorganised reporting into PSG/AMG/ISG and no longer discloses Industrial end-market revenue separately. However, the directional thesis (industrial weakness pressuring guidance) was not supported by the broader picture: group revenue exceeded the guidance midpoint, Non-GAAP gross margin came in at 38.5%, AI Data Center revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 30%+ sequentially, Q2 guidance was raised, and management explicitly stated 'demand strengthened through the quarter and we have moved beyond the cyclical trough on a path to recovery.' New design wins in industrial energy storage (Sineng 430kW) further suggest constructive end-market dynamics. The mismatch direction (guidance_too_optimistic) is contradicted by the available qualitative and group-level evidence.

assumptions.name: AI/Data Center mix supporting gross margin
assumptions.resolution_note: Non-GAAP gross margin of 38.5% cleared the 38.0% threshold by 50bp. AI Data Center revenue more than doubled YoY and grew 30%+ sequentially, validating the AI/Data Center mix thesis as a margin support factor. Q2 guidance of 38.0–40.0% non-GAAP gross margin signals continued sequential margin expansion.

lessons_learned: Stage 2 self-labeled 'noise' at 45% probability — the marginal 3.2% beat in the opposite direction is well within the calibrated uncertainty band of a noise classification. No methodology damage; system correctly avoided a false signal claim.

The Stage 1 IR-ON-02 material_mismatch was not confirmed at resolution. Diagnostic root cause: peer evidence base used in the analysis (Infineon Q1 FY26, ST Q4'25, NXP Q4'25, Microchip Q3 FY26) was structurally one quarter older than the resolution period. Cyclical recovery turn occurred in the intervening weeks, and aggregate-level peer pessimism overshadowed sub-segment recovery signals (Microchip 'broad-based recovery' language, NXP 'improving demand environment') that were present but underweighted in the F/I/S aggregation.

The case has been formally documented as the empirical basis for the v1.3.0 protocol patch (Peer Recency Classification and Peer Trajectory Check) and the v2.0.0 architecture revision (introduction of Stage 2 Challenge phase between assumption analysis and consensus scaling).

Segment reporting reorganisation (Auto/Industrial/Other → PSG/AMG/ISG) made two of three testable questions formally unresolvable against their original thresholds. Future analyses should flag announced segment restructurings ahead of the resolution period and adjust testable question framing accordingly.

Pipeline behaviour confirmed: the Stage 1 mismatch was directionally incorrect but Stage 2 (segment scaling and noise classification) prevented this from propagating to a public-facing signal. The dampening architecture worked as designed.

score_summary.stage2_note: Industrial segment share 28.9% scaled the -17pp assumption-level mismatch down to -4.9pp at group level, producing a 45% surprise probability classified as noise. Group EPS came in at $0.64 vs consensus $0.62 — a 3.2% beat that is directionally opposite to the predicted miss but within calibrated uncertainty for a noise-labeled call. The Stage 1 mismatch direction was not confirmed; the Stage 2 noise classification was correctly restrained. Net: directional miss at Stage 2 with no calibration damage; methodological lesson on peer evidence recency captured in lessons_learned.

assumptions.mismatch_drivers: GE Vernova Wind Q1 2026: -25% revenue, EBITDA loss $382M — US onshore remains weak, tariffs and permitting weigh on sector. Nordex Q1 2026 order intake fell YoY. Siemens Gamesa Q1 positive margin partly attributed to timing effects by management itself. External wind market improving but not broadly enough to support FY2026 break-even path with confidence.

score_summary.stage2_note: Gamesa segment share 24.3% scales -20pp assumption-level mismatch down to -4.9pp at group level. Gas Services and Grid Technologies externally well-supported — Gamesa is the isolated blind spot. Strongest assumption-level mismatch in the portfolio (-20pp) but compensated by strong peer segments.

entries.subject: ASML Holding NV

assumptions.name: Export control risk
assumptions.miss_reason: MATCH Act appeared April 2026, after quarter-end March 29. Driver had no mechanical impact on Q1 numbers.

lessons_learned: Generic cycle skepticism against a well-understood mega-trend (AI/EUV) rarely constitutes a genuine edge.
Timing mismatch between driver appearance and quarter-end is a fixable methodological error — now addressed by driver_timing field.
Two correct aligned-calls (IR-ASML-01, IR-ASML-02) confirm guidance robustness and have real value.
